paper_title: InitFree-SfM: When Initialization-Free Bundle Adjustment meets Learned Structure-from-Motion

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is a very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where a good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, a low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing a gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFree-SfM, a complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose a simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play a central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements.

sections.title: Abstract
sections.content: Initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA) aims to jointly recover camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial global estimate. It is very challenging problem, especially compared to traditional BA where good estimation is assumed. While recent methods optimize surrogate Object Space Error (OSE) objectives from random initialization, low objective value does not necessarily yield an accurate reconstruction, revealing gap between optimization and reconstruction. We show that existing InitFree BA pipelines struggle to produce accurate 3D reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks, and demonstrate that incorporating learned metric depth substantially improves their practical feasibility. We introduce InitFreeSfM1, complete initialization-free SfM pipeline combining learned correspondences, metric depth, depth-consistent track construction, and joint metric refinement. Within this framework, we propose simple depth-augmented OSE (dOSE), which complements the directional constraints of OSE by constraining landmark positions along their viewing rays. Our approach substantially outperforms existing InitFree BA methods and achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Importantly, our analysis challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, revealing that geometric constraints play central role in accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based optimization provides further improvements. 1. Introduction The joint optimization of camera poses and scene landmarks, known as bundle adjustment (BA), is central comIn ponent of structure-from-motion (SfM) pipelines [6]. 1Project page: https : / / github . com / simonwebertum / initfree-sfm.git its traditional formulation [24], BA is used as refinement stage, after suitable initial estimates of the camera poses and scene structure have been obtained, typically through sequence of geometric steps such as relative pose estimation, rotation averaging, and triangulation. recent line of work [9, 10, 17, 34] challenges this paradigm by considering BA with random initialization. This setting, referred to as initialization-free bundle adjustment (InitFree BA), seeks to jointly optimize global camera poses and scene landmarks without requiring an initial estimate of either. To tackle this challenging problem, existing methods typically adopt three-stage pipeline: (i) surrogate Object Space Error (OSE), combined with regularization, is optimized using variable projection (VarPro); (ii) camera parameters and landmarks are refined by minimizing reprojection error; and (iii) metric upgrade [20] is applied to recover Euclidean camera poses from relaxed camera matrices in R34. Despite this promising optimization framework, recent experimental evidence [32] reveals substantial gap between optimization and reconstruction: existing OSE-based pipelines can converge to low surrogate objective values while producing geometrically inaccurate reconstructions. This discrepancy arises from insufficient geometric constraints during optimization and the instability of the subsequent metric upgrade. Consequently, successful surrogate optimization does not necessarily translate into accurate reconstruction, as will be further illustrated in App. A. At the same time, recent advances in learned geometry offer an opportunity to revisit this problem. Monocular depth foundation models provide geometric information that complements classical multi-view constraints. While OSE encourages reconstructed landmarks to lie along their observed viewing rays, predicted depth additionally constrains their positions along these rays. More generally, learned geometric priors provide information that can be exploited throughout the reconstruction pipeline, rather than 1 (a) Sparse SfM comparison: delivery area (b) Comparison with feed-forward methods: playground (a) pOSE (LoMa), GLOMAP (LoMa), Figure 1. This raises natural question: Can learned geometric priors bridge the gap between optimization and reconstruction in initialization-free BA? In this work, we investigate this question by introducing InitFree-SfM, complete structure-from-motion pipeline built around initialization-free joint optimization. We integrate learned correspondences and monocular metric depth through depth-consistent correspondence filtering, initialization-free OSE-based optimization, and joint metric refinement. In particular, we revisit the classical OSE formulation by introducing simple depth-augmented objective (dOSE), and directly optimize camera poses on SE(3) using variable projection, avoiding the need for subsequent metric upgrade. Finally, we jointly refine the reconstruction using image observations, predicted depths, and pairwise geometric constraints. Our experiments demonstrate that the resulting pipeline substantially improves reconstruction accuracy over existing InitFree BA approaches, whose conventional optimization and metric-upgrade procedures often fail on modern datasets. Moreover, InitFree-SfM achieves competitive accuracy with established SfM pipelines, including on challenging low-overlap image collections. Surprisingly, we find that joint metric refinement can already recover accurate reconstructions directly from random initialization, without any intermediate OSE optimization. This challenges the prevailing emphasis on surrogate objectives in previous InitFree BA research, suggesting that the availability of geometric constraints is the primary driver of accurate reconstruction, while OSE-based initialization provides additional improvements. Revisiting initialization-free BA. We demonstrate that existing initialization-free BA formulations often fail to produce accurate reconstructions on modern SfM benchmarks. We show that incorporating learned depth information throughout the reconstruction pipeline substantially improves their practical applicability. complete initialization-free SfM pipeline. We intro2 Figure 2. Overview of InitFree-SfM. Starting from input images, we extract pairwise correspondences and monocular metric depth, followed by geometric consistency filtering (Secs. 4.1 and 4.2). From random global initialization, dOSE jointly optimizes camera poses and 3D landmarks (Sec. 3.2), followed by joint metric refinement incorporating depth and relative pose constraints to obtain the final 3D reconstruction (Sec. 4.3). Overall, our simple yet effective pipeline offers new perspective on initialization-free BA, highlighting the central role of geometric constraints beyond surrogate objective optimization. duce InitFree-SfM, combining learned correspondences, monocular metric depth, depth-consistent correspondence filtering, initialization-free joint optimization directly on SE(3), and joint metric refinement. We additionally propose simple depth-augmented Object Space Error (dOSE) that retains the variable-projection structure of existing formulations. New insights into initialization-free reconstruction. Contrary to the emphasis on surrogate objective design in previous work, we show that accurate reconstruction can be achieved through joint metric refinement directly from random initialization, without an OSE stage. Our experiments highlight the central role of geometric constraints, while demonstrating that dOSE further improves reconstruction accuracy. Competitive reconstruction accuracy. We demonstrate substantial improvements over existing InitFree BA approaches and competitive performance against modern SfM pipelines on ETH3D, LaMAR, and challenging lowoverlap benchmarks. We hope that our novel formulation and promising experimental results will open new perspectives on the challenging and still relatively unexplored problem of initialization-free bundle adjustment. 2. Related Work As our approach bridges feasible structure-from-motion to initialization-free bundle adjustment, we review works on recent SfM pipelines and on InitFree BA. Traditional and feed-forward structure-from-motion Traditional SfM pipelines recover camera poses and scene structure through sequence of geometric operations, including feature matching, relative pose estimation, triangulation, and bundle adjustment [6]. Incremental approaches, such as COLMAP [22], progressively register images and reconstruct landmarks, while global approaches, such as GLOMAP [18], estimate camera poses jointly from pairwise geometric constraints. Recent advances in learned geometry bridge SfM pipelines to learned feature matching and monocular geometric priors. Methods such as VGGSfM [25] integrate learned components into incremental reconstruction, while MP-SfM [19] exploits monocular surface priors to improve robustness under limited image overlap. Recently, feed-forward approaches such as Dust3r [28], VGGT [26], π3 [29], and Depth Anything 3 [14] directly predict multi-view geometry from images through single pass. Despite these advances, recovering accurate 3D reconstructions by jointly optimizing camera poses and scene structure directly from random initialization remains largely unexplored. Initialization-free bundle adjustment. InitFree BA aims to jointly recover global camera poses and scene structure without requiring an initial estimate of their global configuration (see App. for formal definition). The problem, linked to the photogrammetry community [5], is relatively novel, and highly challenging. Early work demonstrated that projective BA could be optimized from arbitrary initialization using variable projection algorithm [7], exploiting the separable structure of the Object Space Error (OSE). Subsequent approaches, including pOSE [34], RpOSE [9], expOSE [10], pOSE+rot [17], improve the optimization of OSE-based objectives through different regularizations. Weber et al [31] extend the InitFree BA problem to large-scale datasets. However, these methods have primarily focused on the optimization problem itself, rather than its integration into complete SfM pipeline. Moreover, recent experimental study [32] highlights substantial discrepancy between minimizing surrogate OSE objectives and recovering accurate reconstructions, particularly due to the subsequent metric upgrade. Despite their theoretical appeal, the potential of InitFree BA for practical SfM remains largely unexplored. Our work revisits this problem from different perspective, emphasizing the role of geometric constraints in enabling accurate metric reconstruction through initialization-free joint optimization. 3. Experiments We revisit existing InitFree BA pipelines, demonstrating how learned depth and geometric constraints substantially improve geometric reconstruction (Sec. 5.1). We then evaluate InitFree-SfM against established SfM approaches, including on challenging low-overlap datasets (Secs. 5.2 and 5.3). Finally, we conduct ablation studies to assess the contributions of individual components (Sec. 5.4). We report pose AUC@1/5/20, following [18, 26]. For InitFree BA methods, camera rotations are sampled uniformly on SO(3), translations from Gaussian distribution, and landmarks are recovered through VarPro. We give more details, as well as dataset and implementation settings, in App. F. 5.1. Can InitFree BA recover accurate reconstructions? Following common practice [26], we evaluate existing OSE-based InitFree BA methods on 25 ETH3D scenes [23], with up to 20 images each. We consider pOSE [34], expOSE [10], and pOSE+rot [17], progressively examining different optimization and refinement strategies  (Fig. 3)  . The original pipelines, combining relaxed camera optimization in R34, reprojection refinement, and metric upgrade, yield poor accuracy (Fig. 3a). Direct optimization on SE(3) improves accuracy but remains insufficient with Introducing our reprojection-only refinement (Fig. 3b). depth-aware joint metric refinement substantially improves all three OSE formulations (Fig. 3c). Surprisingly, this refinement alone recovers accurate reconstructions directly from random initialization, without any OSE optimization (Fig. 3d). This suggests that geometric constraints during refinement, rather than surrogate OSE optimization alone, are central to accurate reconstruction. Nevertheless, our proposed dOSE further improves accuracy, achieving the best results in this comparison (Fig. 3e). 5.2. Can InitFree-SfM compete with modern SfM pipelines? We evaluate InitFree-SfM on ETH3D [23] and LaMAR [21], comparing against (COLMAP, VGincremental feed-forward (VGGT, π3, DA3), and global GSfM), (GLOMAP) SfM methods, as well as pOSE [34]. As shown in Tab. 1, InitFree-SfM achieves the highest AUC@20 on both ETH3D and LaMAR, demonstrating strong overall reconstruction accuracy. While traditional SfM methods remain more accurate at the strictest 1 threshold, our results highlight the potential of initialization-free joint optimization to recover competitive accuracy. How robust is InitFree-SfM to reduced image overlap? We evaluate InitFree-SfM on low-overlap subsets of ETH3D [23] and SMERF [2], following the protocol of [19]. We consider both sparse (LoMa [16]) and dense (RoMa v2 [4]) matchers, and include MP-SfM [19], specifically designed for low-overlap reconstruction, among our baselines. As shown on Tab. 2, on ETH3D, InitFree-SfM achieves the second-best accuracy in 23 out of 24 comparisons across overlap levels, accuracy thresholds, and matchers, while requiring substantially less computation than the leading MP-SfM method  (Fig. 4)  . On SMERF, InitFreeSfM also achieves the second-best accuracy in 10 out of 24 comparisons, although the performance gap to MP-SfM is larger, particularly with sparse correspondences. This coincides with more fragmented graphs of verified relative pose constraints (54% for SMERF against 68% for ETH3D lowoverlap after depth-checking in the filtering with LoMa). These results show that InitFree-SfM remains competitive under challenging low-overlap conditions, offering favorable accuracyruntime trade-off, particularly on ETH3D. 5.4. Ablation study Robustness to the matcher. Tab. 3 demonstrates the robustness of InitFree-SfM across wide range of correspondence extractors, from sparse to dense matchers. While RoMa v2 achieves the best results on ETH3D and MASt3R on LaMAR, our pipeline remains competitive across different matching strategies. Robustness to the depth estimator. Tab. 4 evaluates the impact of different monocular depth foundation models. The results remain consistent across MoGe-2, MoGe-3, and DA3. This suggests that our approach does not rely on particular depth estimator. Figure 4. Runtime comparison on low-overlap ETH3D (left) and SMERF (right). Lower is better. InitFree-SfM offers favorable accuracy-runtime trade-off, achieving competitive reconstruction accuracy at substantially lower computational cost than MP-SfM. All methods use LoMa; runtimes are averaged per subset. Contribution of individual components. As shown in Tab. 5, depth-consistent filtering and geometric priors improve reconstruction accuracy. Joint metric refinement is particularly important: removing it causes substantial performance drop. Although refinement alone achieves competitive accuracy from random initialization, initializing it with dOSE further improves the results. Additional lowoverlap experiments in App. confirm this benefit, with larger gains on SMERF. Uncalibrated approach. On LaMAR, accuracy reaches 63.44%, comparable to uncalibrated GLOMAP (64.15%) and approaching VGGT (69.95%). Conclusion We revisit initialization-free BA by investigating how recent advances in learned metric geometry can enable accurate 3D reconstruction from random initialization. Building on this insight, we introduce InitFree-SfM, complete SfM pipeline combining learned metric geometry with depthaugmented Object Space Error, recovering camera poses and scene structure without subsequent metric upgrade. Our analysis highlights the central role of geometric conFigure 5. Effect of calibration on ETH3D and LaMAR. Calibrated runs use dataset intrinsics; uncalibrated runs use MoGe-2 intrinsics for ours and native calibration estimation for GLOMAP. straints in accurate reconstruction, alongside the benefits of dOSE optimization. Experiments demonstrate substantial improvements over prevailing InitFree BA methods and competitive accuracy with modern SfM pipelines, even under low overlap. Overall, our findings offer promising perspective on InitFree BA, hopefully encouraging further 8 research into this challenging, largely unexplored problem. Limitations and future work. Our method benefits from known camera calibration, motivating improvements in uncalibrated reconstruction. Scaling to larger image collections and exploring additional geometric priors remain promising directions. 7. LLM usage statement LLMs were not used to generate research ideas and content of the related work. ChatGPT-6 Luna was used to polish the manuscript (grammar and writing) after an initial draft entirely written by the authors, generate code following our instructions, aggregate experimental results into tables (Tab. 15), generate bar plots  (Fig. 35)  and edit the visualization in Fig. 2.

App. investigates additional OSE formulations with relative rotation constraints. A. Convergence vs Reconstruction Gap Consistent with the experimental analysis of Weber et al. [32], we observe discrepancy between surrogate optimization and metric reconstruction quality in existing OSEbased formulation. As shown in Fig. 6, the pOSE objective decreases substantially on two ETH3D scenes, yet the final camera poses and scene structure remain inaccurate after reprojection refinement and metric upgrade. These examples illustrate that successful reduction of the OSE objective alone does not ensure an accurate metric reconstruction. B. Formal Definition of InitFree BA Following the initialization-free BA literature, we use initialization-free to mean that optimization does not require an accurate initial global reconstruction: camera poses and landmark coordinates can start from random values [9, 10, 17, 34]. This concerns the initialization of the unknowns, rather than the absence of geometric information in the input or objective. This distinction is consistent with previous work. The original pOSE paper [34] explicitly identifies robust matching and relative-pose verification as upstream stages of SfM. RpOSE and expOSE [9, 10] focus on reconstruction from given image measurements, leaving correspondence extraction outside their optimization problem; this does not exclude geometric verification upstream. More explicitly, pOSE+rot [17] incorporates relative rotation estimates into its objective, with weights derived from two-view reprojection optimization involving relative translation and local structure. Likewise, our method uses image-derived pairwise constraints to guide optimization, but does not convert them Table 6. Effect of correspondence filtering with LoMa and MoGe2. It is therefore initialization-free in the sense established by previous work, while explicitly incorporating geometric measurements into the objective. C. Effect of OSE-based optimization on lowoverlap problems Although joint refinement from random initialization already produces meaningful reconstructions, dOSE initialization improves accuracy at all three thresholds in every low-overlap group  (Fig. 7)  . For instance, at AUC@20, the gains range from 4.87.9 percentage points on ETH3D and 12.922.0 points on SMERF. These results show that OSE-based optimization provides useful geometric guidance beyond the constraints already present in joint refinement, with particularly substantial benefits on SMERF. D. Implementation details. For each image pair, we compute the angular discrepancy between its depth-derived relative rotation and the rotation implied by the strongestedge spanning tree, and pairs with discrepancy greater than τR = 15 are rejected. We optimize dOSE using VarPro for at most 60 iterations. We approximate the Huber depth penalty using IRLS, fixing robust weights during each VarPro elimination and updating them after accepted steps, starting after the first continuation stage. We employ depth-weight continuation schedule, following the general principle of progressively transitioning toward the target objective [1]. Specifically, the weight λd is progressively increased to 5%, 25%, and 100% of its target value λd = 30 over three 20-iteration stages. Note that we selected λd = 30 during preliminary experiments and retained it throughout the subsequent evaluations, without dataset-specific tuning. During the last stage, optimization terminates early when the objective decrease satisfies Eold Enew < 109 max(1, Enew). The resulting reconstruction undergoes joint metric refinement using LevenbergMarquardt algorithm and preconditioned conjugate gradients, with 30-iteration warm-up followed by at most 120 refinement iterations. Each refinement stage terminates early if the relative parameter update falls below 108 or the relative objective decrease falls below 1010. Both optimizers also terminate upon persistent step rejection when the damping parameter reaches 1012. Dataset selection. For ETH3D [23], we evaluate 25 scenes using up to 20 images per scene, selected at uniformly spaced indices in the filename-sorted image list; scenes with fewer than 20 images use all available images. Using fixed random seed, we select one temporally contiguous window per capture. Reference poses are used only during subset construction to exclude abrupt motion and near-static windows: consecutive frames must be within 3 m, 45, and 5 s, and each window must include at least 0.5 displacement from its first camera. All methods receive the same frozen image selections. For low-overlap ETH3D and SMERF, we follow the released MP-SfM benchmark subsets and overlap groups [19]. Evaluation metric. Following current practice, we define joint pose error as the maximum of the relative rotation error and the sign-invariant translation-direction error for each camera pair. We report the area under the recall curve (AUC) up to 1, 5, and 20, normalized to percentages. Baseline configurations. For Depth Anything 3, we use DA3-Large-1.1; for MP-SfM, we use the Metric3Dv2 Giant preset for depth and normal estimation. In the main ETH3D and LaMAR comparisons, LoMa-based methods use LoMa-B with 2048 keypoints per image and confidence threshold of 0.10. In the low-overlap comparisons, our method and GLOMAP use LoMa-B with 4096 keypoints. For the RoMa-v2 comparisons, we use the precise preset and sample 1024 correspondences per image pair. Geometric methods use dataset calibration in the calibrated comparisons, while feed-forward methods and VGGSfM estimate their own calibration. More sophisticated OSE Inspired by pOSE+rot [17], we investigate augmenting dOSE with relative rotation penalties during VarPro. The penalties use information matrices derived from linearized two-view reprojection optimization, accounting for the local translation and landmark parameters. Unlike our default pipeline, which introduces pairwise geometric constraints during joint refinement, this variant also incorporates rotation information in the initial dOSE stage.
